scientific_hypothesis: For a two-layer antireflection coating on glass (n=1.52) using SiO2 (n=1.46) and TiO2 (n=2.40), placing the higher-index TiO2 layer adjacent to the incident medium (Air) and the lower-index SiO2 layer adjacent to the substrate yields a lower broadband mean reflectance than the reverse order, given the specific thickness constraints of 40-160 nm.
expected_advantages: Potentially better impedance matching at the air interface due to higher initial index step
Different interference phase conditions may align better with the 40-160 nm constraint window than the SiO2-first configuration
known_risks: The high index contrast at the Air/TiO2 interface might dominate losses if the SiO2 layer cannot sufficiently compensate
The optimal thicknesses might fall outside the 40-160 nm bound, limiting performance
expected_observations: best_target_score should increase as the optimizer converges towards the global minimum within the thickness bounds
valid_candidates should remain equal to the number of evaluated points if all thickness pairs satisfy the 40-160 nm constraint
tightest_margin should reflect the distance of the best solution from the 40 nm or 160 nm boundaries
If the hypothesis holds, the final mean reflectance should be lower than typical single-layer limits, potentially approaching the 0.03 target
stop_conditions: if best_target_score improves by less than 1e-4 against the historical best for two consecutive rounds, treat the axis as exhausted, stop and keep the current best
if valid_candidates drops to zero due to constraint violations (unlikely given bounded search space), stop and report failure
